label: MC420L 10G SFP+ media converter (multi-gig copper)
description: Media converter bridging a 1G/2.5G/5G/10GBASE-T copper port to an SFP+ cage, with a DIP switch that selects whether the optical side runs at 1G/10G or 2.5G. Two ports, one collision domain each way - a bridge, not a switch.
notes: TP-Link datasheet: '1x 1G/2.5G/5G/10Gbps Auto-Negotiation RJ45 port supporting Auto-MDI/MDIX', optical port 'SFP+' with 'Easy switching between 1G/10G and 2.5G optical port modes' via DIP switch, IEEE 802.3ab/bz/an/z/ae/aq/cb. The optical cage is declared with speedCaps [1000, 2500, 10000] rather than 5G because the DIP switch only offers 1G/10G and 2.5G - 5GBASE-T exists on the copper side only, which is a real trap when someone puts a 5G link on the fibre side and wonders why it drops to 2.5G. Copper media: 1000BASE-T/2.5G/5G on Cat5e+ to 100 m, 10GBASE-T on Cat6 to 55 m or Cat6a to 100 m. 9V/0.6A external adapter, 5.26 W, 94.5 x 73 x 27 mm, standalone or in the Omada MC1400 chassis. Maximum reach depends entirely on the SFP+ module fitted, so no reach is claimed here.
